title: Train Wheels Have No Steering. So How Do Trains Turn?
lines: Train wheels have no steering. So how do trains turn?
The two wheels are locked to one solid axle, so they always spin together.
But on a curve, the outer rail is longer than the inner one.
The secret is the shape. The wheels are cones, wider on the inside.
On a curve, the wheels slide outward a little.
Now the outer wheel rolls on its wide part, and the inner wheel on its narrow part.
So each turn of the outer wheel covers more distance, and the train steers itself.
That's why train wheels are cone-shaped. Follow for more!
caption:
Train wheels can't steer, and both are locked to the same axle 🚆 The trick is that they're slightly cone-shaped: on a curve the outer wheel rolls on a bigger diameter and the train turns by itself. (Shape exaggerated in the animation.)
